value.body: The Indian Forest Service (IFoS) is an All India Service that manages forests, wildlife and protected areas. UPSC recruits through the Indian Forest Service Examination, whose preliminary stage is the same as the Civil Services prelims. Officers are trained at the Indira Gandhi National Forest Academy, Dehradun, and allotted to state cadres.

items.label: Mains
items.note: General English, General Knowledge, and two optional subjects of two papers each, then an interview

items.label: Attempts
items.note: More for OBC; unlimited within age for SC/ST

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree with at least one of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Science, Botany, Chemistry, Geology, Mathematics, Physics, Statistics or Zoology, or a degree in Agriculture, Forestry or Engineering. Apply in the common UPSC form; you take the Civil Services prelims, and a separate (higher) cut-off decides who goes to the IFoS mains. A physical standards and walking test is also required.

value.title: At a glance
items: Competition is very high: lakhs sit the common prelims for a few hundred posts across both exams.
The optional subjects are science-based, so a science or engineering background is directly useful.
Postings are often in remote and forested areas, with field work and law-enforcement duties.
Preparation commonly takes one to several years.

value.title: IFoS vacancies notified by year
value.note: Approximate vacancies stated in each year's notice; UPSC says these can change, and final selections can differ (e.g. 147 recommended in 2023).
value.source: UPSC IFoS examination notices, as reported (PW, Vajiram & Ravi)
